destination.name: Tennant Creek
destination.tagline: A gold-mining town on the Stuart Highway, halfway between Alice Springs and Darwin.
destination.description: Tennant Creek is a town of about 3,500 people on the edge of the Barkly Tableland, roughly 500 km north of Alice Springs. Gold found in 1925 created the township, and the Battery Hill Mining Centre keeps that history alive with underground tours. The Warumungu are the traditional custodians, and Nyinkka Nyunyu and the sacred Kunjarra tell their story. The Stuart Highway links it to the Devils Marbles to the south.
whyVisit: Tour a gold mine at Battery Hill

goodToKnow.title: Station key from Battery Hill
goodToKnow.detail: The Telegraph Station buildings are locked: collect the key at Battery Hill on Peko Road, which is also the visitor centre.

goodToKnow.title: Check roads first
goodToKnow.detail: The Pebbles is 6 km of unsealed road and floods can close roads in the Wet. Check conditions before heading out.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The cooler months, {months}, suit sightseeing: summer days are very hot and floods can cut roads.
